# Account

`sales.obj.core.account` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> The customer-facing relationship with one organisation, spanning every deal, contact and contract with it. Distinct from Company: Company is what the organisation IS, Account is our relationship WITH it. Conflating them is why expansion looks like new business and churn looks like a lost deal — both errors flow from having one record that carries firmographics and relationship state in the same fields. The test is ownership of the fact: employee count is true whether or not we exist, so it belongs to Company; who owns the relationship, what has been signed, and whether the last renewal was fought over are facts about us and belong here. One company may carry several accounts — subsidiaries, regions, business units — and the reverse is never true.


Also called: `Customer Account`, `Client`, `Named Account`

| `churned` | Contract ended without renewal. Distinct from a lost deal — a lost deal on a customer leaves them a customer. | — |  |

## Constraints

- **`ac.one_company_per_account`** An account references exactly one company. Many accountsto one company is legitimate; the reverse is a data error that double-counts pipeline.
- **`ac.no_firmographics_here`** Employee count, industry, revenue and technology are factsabout the organisation and must live on Company. Any such field appearing on Account is the conflation this object exists to prevent.
- **`ac.stage_cannot_regress_past_customer`** relationship_stage may not move from customerback to prospect or opportunity. The only exit from customer is churned.
- **`ac.churn_requires_contract_end`** relationship_stage = churned requires a contractthat ended unrenewed, not a lost deal.


## Business rules

- **`ac.account_requires_a_company`** An account with no company_ref cannot be scored for ICP fit or territory assignment. Fit is a property of the organisation; without the link there is nothing to score against.

- **`ac.expansion_is_not_new_business`** A deal on an account in relationship_stage customer, expansion or at_risk must be reported as expansion revenue, never as new business. The two carry different costs of acquisition and different win rates, and mixing them makes both numbers meaningless.

- **`ac.churn_is_not_a_lost_deal`** Losing a deal on an existing customer must not move relationship_stage to churned. They remain a customer with a contract until that contract ends unrenewed. Treating the two as one event both overstates churn and hides it, in different quarters.

- **`ac.renewal_dates_bound_the_plan`** An account with a populated renewal_at and no plan working backwards from it is unmanaged. Renewals are lost in the quarter before they are decided, not in the week they fall due.

- **`ac.single_threaded_account`** An account with one edge and a live deal is single-threaded. On a customer account this is worse than on a prospect, because the entire renewal rests on one person's continued employment.

- **`ac.silent_customer_is_not_a_happy_customer`** A customer account with no inbound contact for several reply-cadence multiples must be surfaced. Satisfied customers are quiet in a different way from departing ones, and the pipeline cannot tell them apart, so a human must look.

## Actions

- **Build the account plan backwards from renewal_at** (human) — The date is fixed by paper we already have. Planning forwards from today is how renewals arrive as surprises.
- **Open a second independent relationship** (human) — In a different reporting line, or it is not a second thread. This is the only durable defence against a champion leaving.
- **Secure an executive sponsor** (human) — Someone seniorwho would take the call if things went wrong. Cheap to arrange while the relationship is healthy and impossible afterwards.
- **Run a displacement defence** (human) — Different play from a competitive new-business deal: the incumbent advantage is real but only if used before procurement formalises the comparison.
- **Qualify an expansion into a new department** (human) — Treat it as a new sale with a warm reference, not as an upsell. The new department has its own budget, its own stakeholders and no loyalty to us.
- **Request a reference** (human) — Doubles as the cheapestavailable satisfaction test. A polite refusal is data.

## Metrics

- **net_revenue_retention** (percent) — Expansion minus churn over the base. Computableonly if expansion and new business are separable, which is this object's whole job.
- **logo_retention** (percent) —
- **expansion_rate** (percent) — Share of customer accounts with a live expansiondeal.
- **single_threaded_customer_share** (percent) — Customer accounts with one relationship.The number that predicts churn best and is watched least.
- **time_to_second_purchase** (days) — customer_since to the second signed contract.The clearest measure of whether onboarding worked.
- **account_response_latency** (hours) — Inbound latency across the relationship,against its own baseline.


## Examples

- **Prospect account with three open deals across two divisions** — relationship_stage opportunity,never customer. Three deals do not make a customer; a signature does.
- **Customer buying a second product** — relationship_stage expansion. Reported as new businessby most CRMs, which is precisely the error the Account/Company split exists to prevent.
- **Customer who lost a competitive deal for a new module** — Still a customer. A lost dealhere is not churn, and recording it as churn both overstates the churn number and hides the real one.
- **One company, three accounts — EMEA, Federal, and the acquired subsidiary** — Separatebudgets, separate stakeholders, separate renewals. Merging them to tidy the CRM destroys the only view in which one is healthy and another is leaving.
- **Silent account, renewal in six weeks, no executive sponsor** — THE classic misread.Reads as low-maintenance and green on every dashboard because nothing bad has been observed — and nothing at all has been observed.

> Five of ten patterns are executable; five are blocked. The highest-value signal gap is derived.account_open_deal_count, or any account-scoped aggregate at all — every one of the twelve substrate fact paths is deal- or thread-scoped, so the engine cannot count the deals, contacts or contracts belonging to an account. That single absence is the root of three separate degradations in this file: expansion cannot be distinguished from new business, coverage falls back to raw graph degree, and account recency is approximated from whichever deal happens to be busiest. Second-ranked is the contract_signed observation kind, shared with Decision Maker and Company: the prospect-to-customer transition, the most consequential in the object, currently has to be typed in by hand.
